speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a pruritic rash on both upper arms; to help me determine the cause, can you tell me when this rash first appeared and if you have noticed any changes in your temperature or breathing?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Scabies (specifically crusted or extensive scabies given the 5-month duration and bilateral upper extremity involvement).

I have noted the chronic, worsening nature of the rash over five months without resolution and your denial of new exposures. Before confirming this, I need to rule out other causes like allergic contact dermatitis or drug eruptions; could you please confirm if any household members or close contacts are also experiencing itching or a rash? REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy of the rash focusing on wrist flexor creases and interdigital spaces.
